A real-time 3D visualization of the electric and magnetic fields of a moving positive point charge, computed directly from the Lienard-Wiechert potentials. Retardation is exact: field points see the charge's position, velocity, and acceleration at the retarded time found by solving the light-cone equation against the charge's recorded trajectory, so kinks in the field visibly propagate outward at speed $c$ whenever the charge suddenly accelerates.

Pick a preset motion (circular or oscillating, around any axis) to see radiation patterns, or let it meander (a random walk splined through waypoints confined to a ball around the origin). You can also drag the charge directly with your mouse (confined to the basis plane of whichever slice orientation is selected). The crimson arrow at the charge shows its instantaneous acceleration.

Drag on empty space to orbit the camera or enable "Auto orbit". Change the view to "2D" to see the waves that travel along 1 dimension of the axes.
